note: Review-only companion; not a TestsData row. Full distractor-specific and technical final review still recommended before live insert.

questions.text: Which component executes machine instructions?
questions.rationale: The CPU executes instructions.

questions.text: Which component connects the CPU, memory and expansion devices?
questions.rationale: The motherboard provides the main interconnection platform.

questions.text: Which memory is normally volatile?
questions.rationale: RAM normally loses contents when power is removed.

questions.text: Which component stores data magnetically on rotating platters?
questions.rationale: An HDD records data magnetically on rotating platters.

questions.text: Which port is commonly used to transmit digital video and audio to a display?
questions.rationale: HDMI carries digital audio/video.

questions.text: Which device is an input peripheral?
questions.rationale: A keyboard sends user input to the computer.

questions.text: Which is an output peripheral?
questions.rationale: A monitor displays visual output.

questions.text: What is the primary role of a computer power supply unit?

options.label: D
options.text: Convert mains power into suitable DC outputs for components

questions.rationale: The PSU provides regulated DC power to internal components.

questions.text: What does BIOS traditionally help the computer do during startup?

options.label: A
options.text: Initialize hardware and begin the boot process

questions.rationale: BIOS firmware initializes platform hardware and starts booting.

questions.text: Which connector standard is commonly used for general-purpose peripherals such as flash drives?
questions.rationale: USB is a common interface for many peripherals.

questions.text: Which keyboard switch type generally uses individual mechanical switches?
questions.rationale: Mechanical keyboards use discrete mechanical switches.

questions.text: Which display technology uses a cathode-ray tube?
questions.rationale: CRT uses an electron beam and phosphor screen.

questions.text: Which printer is typically an impact printer?
questions.rationale: A dot-matrix printer strikes an ink ribbon against paper.

questions.text: Which printer produces output by spraying small ink droplets?
questions.rationale: Inkjet printers eject tiny drops of ink.

questions.text: Which mouse technology detects movement using light and an optical sensor?
questions.rationale: An optical mouse uses optical sensing rather than a rolling ball.

questions.text: Which device converts sound into an electrical input for a computer?
questions.rationale: A microphone captures sound as input.

questions.text: Which storage type uses laser-based reading from a disc?
questions.rationale: CDs and DVDs are optical storage media.

questions.text: Which is a flash-memory storage device?
questions.rationale: USB flash drives store data in flash memory.

questions.text: Which measure describes the maximum amount of data a drive can store?
questions.rationale: Capacity describes how much data can be stored.

questions.text: Which measure concerns the time needed to access requested data?
questions.rationale: Access time measures the delay before data access.

questions.text: Which device connects to expansion slots on a motherboard?
questions.rationale: Expansion cards fit compatible motherboard expansion slots.

questions.text: Which port traditionally connects a PS/2 keyboard or mouse?
questions.rationale: PS/2 is a legacy keyboard/mouse interface.

questions.text: Which interface commonly uses a 9-pin D-sub connector on older computers?
questions.rationale: Legacy serial COM interfaces commonly used a DE-9 connector.

questions.text: Which older port was designed to transfer multiple data bits in parallel?
questions.rationale: A parallel port transfers multiple bits across separate data lines.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a cooling fan in a laptop?

options.label: A
options.text: Move air to help remove heat

questions.rationale: The fan supports cooling by moving air through the system.

questions.text: Which part supplies portable power when a laptop is unplugged?
questions.rationale: The battery supplies energy when external power is absent.

questions.text: What does a graphics card primarily support?
questions.rationale: A graphics card processes graphics and provides display output.

questions.text: What is a disk partition?

options.label: B
options.text: A logical division of a storage device

questions.rationale: Partitions divide a physical storage device into logical regions.

questions.text: What is normally done by formatting a partition for use with an operating system?

options.label: C
options.text: Prepare a file system on it

questions.rationale: Formatting creates file-system structures for data storage.

questions.text: What is a safe first step before repartitioning a drive containing important files?

options.label: A
options.text: Back up the files and verify the intended disk

questions.rationale: Partitioning can destroy data; a backup and target check reduce risk.

questions.text: Which removable card format is named in the storage syllabus?
questions.rationale: SD is a flash-memory card format.

questions.text: Which device is intended to produce a paper copy of a computer document?
questions.rationale: A printer produces hard-copy output.

questions.text: Which port is commonly used to connect a monitor to a computer?
questions.rationale: Video interfaces carry visual output to a display.

questions.text: Which component usually provides the physical connection points for CPU and memory?
questions.rationale: The motherboard contains sockets/slots for core components.

questions.text: Which device is commonly used for sound output?
questions.rationale: A speaker outputs audio.

questions.text: Which device captures printed pages as digital images?
questions.rationale: A scanner digitizes documents or images.

questions.text: Which part directly performs arithmetic and logical operations as part of instruction execution?
questions.rationale: The processor performs arithmetic, logic and instruction control.

questions.text: Which storage medium is typically read optically?
questions.rationale: A DVD is an optical disc.

questions.text: Which item is an internal hardware component rather than an external peripheral?
questions.rationale: RAM modules are installed internally on the motherboard.

questions.text: What should generally be done before opening a desktop case for hardware work?

options.label: B
options.text: Shut down and disconnect power, then follow anti-static precautions

options.label: C
options.text: Keep the system plugged in and running

options.label: D
options.text: Touch the motherboard pins with metal tools

questions.rationale: Disconnecting power and using anti-static precautions lowers electrical and component risks.

questions.text: A PC powers on, but no image appears on the monitor. Which first check best isolates a simple connection issue?

options.label: B
options.text: Check monitor power, selected input and video cable seating

questions.rationale: Power/input/cable checks can identify basic display connection problems.

questions.text: A motherboard has an available compatible expansion slot and a task needs extra graphics capability. Which installation concept applies?

options.label: A
options.text: Place the card in a RAM slot

options.label: B
options.text: Replace the power socket with a serial port

options.label: C
options.text: Install a compatible graphics expansion card

options.label: D
options.text: Connect the monitor to the microphone jack

questions.rationale: A compatible graphics card uses an appropriate motherboard expansion slot.

questions.text: A file server needs more storage capacity but should keep the existing drive. Which syllabus procedure is relevant?

options.label: D
options.text: Install a second hard drive after checking compatibility and power/data connections

questions.rationale: The syllabus includes installation of a second hard drive.

questions.text: An older peripheral offers only a serial interface, while a computer has no built-in serial port. What must be checked before connecting it?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether a suitable compatible interface/adapter and driver are supported

options.label: B
options.text: Whether the monitor brightness is high enough

options.label: D
options.text: Whether a keyboard uses rubber domes

questions.rationale: Interface compatibility and driver support determine whether it can communicate.

questions.text: A printer must create a multi-part form by striking an ink ribbon. Which type best fits that requirement?
questions.rationale: Dot-matrix printers use impact through an ink ribbon.

questions.text: A user sees faint output from an inkjet printer. Which check is more relevant than changing the monitor?

options.label: A
options.text: Inspect ink levels and printhead/nozzle condition

questions.rationale: Ink supply and printhead condition directly affect inkjet output.

questions.text: A keyboard key repeats or fails. Which hardware maintenance sequence is safest?

options.label: A
options.text: Pour liquid into the keyboard while connected

options.label: B
options.text: Disconnect power, inspect/clean according to the keyboard design, then reassemble and test

options.label: C
options.text: Short all pins to test the switch

questions.rationale: Safe cleaning starts with disconnection and uses the appropriate procedure.

questions.text: A laptop overheats during ordinary use and its fan outlet is blocked by fabric. What should be done first?

options.label: D
options.text: Move it to a hard, unobstructed surface and check ventilation

questions.rationale: Unblocking air intake/exhaust helps restore cooling.

questions.text: A storage comparison must consider how quickly data can move after a drive is active. Which metric is most relevant?
questions.rationale: Transfer rate measures data moved per unit time.

questions.text: A storage upgrade must preserve files already on a drive. Which sequence is safest before partition/format operations?

options.label: B
options.text: Delete the backup to avoid confusion

options.label: C
options.text: Back up and verify the target drive and partition before making changes

options.label: D
options.text: Select a partition by capacity alone without checking

questions.rationale: Backup and target verification reduce the risk of destructive mistakes.

questions.text: A laptop runs on AC power but its battery never charges. Which check is most relevant before replacing the motherboard?

options.label: C
options.text: Verify the adapter, charging connector and battery condition using the device's service guidance

questions.rationale: Power adapter, connector and battery checks can isolate common charging faults.

questions.text: A new HDD is physically installed but is absent from File Explorer. What is a reasonable next check?

options.label: D
options.text: Check device/BIOS detection and then confirm disk initialization, partitioning and formatting as appropriate

questions.rationale: A detected drive may still need initialization or a usable partition/file system.

questions.text: A disk shows 1 TB capacity but transfer of large files is slow. Which distinction helps diagnose the measurement?

options.label: A
options.text: Capacity is amount stored; transfer rate is speed of data movement

options.label: B
options.text: Capacity and transfer rate are identical

options.label: D
options.text: A keyboard switch sets the drive speed

questions.rationale: Capacity and transfer rate measure different properties.

questions.text: A computer starts directly into one OS, but a lab task requires a dual-OS setup. What should be planned first?

options.label: B
options.text: Compatibility, disk space, backups and boot configuration for both OS installations

questions.rationale: Dual installation requires planning partitions, compatibility and boot choices.

questions.text: A monitor looks blurry at its native resolution after a settings change. Which step is most appropriate?

options.label: D
options.text: Select a supported resolution suitable for the display and verify cable/input settings

questions.rationale: A supported display mode often restores clear output.

questions.text: A mouse pointer moves erratically on a surface with reflective patterns. What practical check is most relevant for an optical mouse?

options.label: B
options.text: Clean the sensor area and test on a suitable surface

options.label: D
options.text: Change the keyboard from AT to XT

questions.rationale: Optical sensing can be disrupted by dirt or unsuitable surfaces.

questions.text: A user wants the left and right mouse buttons to swap functions for left-handed use. Which approach matches the topic?

options.label: C
options.text: Change mouse-button settings in the operating system

questions.rationale: Mouse buttons can usually be swapped in OS settings.

questions.text: A technician must select a printer type for quiet, non-impact printing of ordinary documents. Which choice best fits the named syllabus examples?
questions.rationale: Inkjet is a non-impact printer type listed in the course.

questions.text: A PC displays repeated boot failure immediately after hardware changes. Which BIOS-level check is most relevant?

options.label: B
options.text: Confirm the intended boot device and whether key hardware is detected

questions.rationale: Boot-device order and hardware detection affect startup.

questions.text: A second hard drive has been connected by data and power cables, but it does not appear in the OS. Which diagnostic order is sensible?

options.label: D
options.text: Check cable/connector seating and firmware detection, then examine OS disk initialization

questions.rationale: Physical/firmware detection should be checked before OS configuration.

questions.text: A technician is asked to replace a PC-XT keyboard with a newer keyboard. What should be checked first?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether the printer uses a ribbon

options.label: B
options.text: Whether the hard disk uses optical storage

questions.rationale: Legacy keyboard types and interfaces may differ.

questions.text: A display panel has a measured resolution of 1920×1080. What do these figures represent?

options.label: A
options.text: Number of pixels horizontally and vertically

options.label: D
options.text: Disk transfer rate and access time

questions.rationale: Resolution is expressed as horizontal by vertical pixel count.

questions.text: The PSU fan is obstructed by dust and the PC shuts down under load. Which explanation is most plausible?

options.label: A
options.text: The parallel port changes CPU instructions

options.label: B
options.text: Restricted cooling can lead to overheating and protective shutdown

options.label: C
options.text: The hard disk is converted to optical storage

options.label: D
options.text: A dusty fan automatically increases disk capacity

questions.rationale: Cooling failure can raise temperatures and lead to thermal shutdown.

questions.text: A hard drive is reported as detected in BIOS, but the OS asks to initialize it. It may contain another user's data. What is the safest action?

options.label: B
options.text: Initialize immediately because detection proves it is empty

options.label: C
options.text: Stop and verify ownership/contents and backup before initializing or formatting

questions.rationale: Initialization or formatting may overwrite existing metadata or make data harder to recover.

questions.text: A component needs a motherboard expansion slot. Which decision is most important before purchase?

options.label: A
options.text: Check that the card's slot/interface and physical size are compatible with the motherboard and case

options.label: B
options.text: Check only the colour of the card

options.label: C
options.text: Choose the widest connector regardless of fit

options.label: D
options.text: Assume all cards use the same slot

questions.rationale: Slot, physical dimensions and system compatibility must match.

questions.text: A dot-matrix printer is selected for a task that needs duplicate forms. Why can the choice make sense?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a type of optical storage

options.label: B
options.text: It produces output by changing monitor pixels

options.label: C
options.text: Impact printing can make impressions through multi-part forms

options.label: D
options.text: It uses no contact with paper

questions.rationale: Impact printers can strike through multi-part forms.

questions.text: A laptop screen remains dark but an external display works. Which next check best narrows the issue?

options.label: D
options.text: Inspect the internal display brightness/output selection and panel connection with appropriate service precautions

questions.rationale: The evidence points toward the internal display path rather than all graphics output.

questions.text: An HDD has adequate storage capacity, but applications feel delayed when accessing small files. Which metric may be especially relevant?
questions.rationale: Access time influences delay before requested data becomes available.

questions.text: A user has a 2.5-inch laptop drive and wants to install an incompatible desktop drive bay device. What should be checked?

options.label: C
options.text: Drive form factor, connector/interface, bay and power compatibility

questions.rationale: Physical size and interface compatibility determine whether a drive can be installed.

questions.text: Two laptop configurations have similar CPUs but different graphics hardware. For graphics-heavy display tasks, which component difference is directly relevant?
questions.rationale: Graphics hardware contributes to graphics processing and display output.

questions.text: A PC has no power indicator after relocation. What should be checked before disassembling it?

options.label: A
options.text: Outlet, power cable and PSU switch/connection

questions.rationale: External power path checks are simple and non-invasive.

questions.text: A monitor flickers only when the video connector is touched. Which issue is most likely worth checking first?
questions.rationale: The symptom changes with connector movement, indicating a connection issue.

questions.text: A user must choose between a magnetic HDD and flash drive for portable file transfer. Which distinction is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: An HDD is an input peripheral

options.label: C
options.text: An HDD uses magnetic storage; a flash drive uses flash memory

options.label: D
options.text: A flash drive is a display technology

questions.rationale: The devices use different storage technologies.

questions.text: A hard drive upgrade requires removing an old drive and installing a replacement. Which step protects against avoidable hardware risk?

options.label: A
options.text: Hot-swap any drive regardless of support

options.label: B
options.text: Touch contacts with a wet cloth

options.label: D
options.text: Shut down, disconnect power and follow the device's service procedure before handling drives

questions.rationale: Safe shutdown and correct handling reduce damage and electrical risk.

questions.text: A user creates partitions on a new blank disk. Which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: A partition is the same as a keyboard connector

options.label: B
options.text: Partitions divide the disk logically; formatting establishes a file system on a partition

options.label: C
options.text: The BIOS is a printer interface

options.label: D
options.text: Formatting increases the physical number of platters

questions.rationale: Partitioning and formatting are different operations.

questions.text: A printer uses a daisy-wheel mechanism. Which print property is most characteristic of this type?

options.label: A
options.text: Display of pixels on a panel

options.label: D
options.text: Impact printing with formed characters on a wheel

questions.rationale: A daisy-wheel printer is a character-based impact printer.

questions.text: A RAM upgrade is physically compatible but is not detected after assembly. Which check should come early?

options.label: A
options.text: Power down and reseat the compatible module in the specified slot; verify compatibility

questions.rationale: Correct seating and compatibility are basic checks for memory detection.

questions.text: A laptop loses charge unusually quickly although the adapter is disconnected. Which component is directly involved in portable energy supply?
questions.rationale: The battery supplies portable energy.

questions.text: The same USB device works through one port but not another. Which diagnostic comparison is sensible?

options.label: C
options.text: Format the drive attached to the port

options.label: D
options.text: Check for damage/connection issues and test the affected port with a known-good device

questions.rationale: A known-good device helps distinguish port issues from a device problem.

questions.text: After cleaning a keyboard, several keys no longer work. What is a sensible next action?

options.label: B
options.text: Disconnect again, inspect correct reassembly and connectors, then test before replacing parts

questions.rationale: Incorrect reassembly or a connector issue can cause the failure.

questions.text: A PC starts but shuts down after several minutes; the PSU fan outlet is blocked and the case is hot. Which explanation and next step best fit the evidence?

options.label: A
options.text: The monitor resolution causes storage failure

options.label: B
options.text: Restricted airflow may cause overheating; power down safely and inspect ventilation/fan operation before further load testing

options.label: D
options.text: The hard disk capacity is too large; format it

questions.rationale: The heat and obstructed airflow indicate a cooling problem; safely remove the obstruction and inspect cooling.

questions.text: A drive upgrade must retain old files and add a second disk. Which sequence best minimizes avoidable data loss?

options.label: A
options.text: Connect the drive while power is on regardless of support

options.label: B
options.text: Format the original first, then check compatibility

options.label: C
options.text: Back up important data, confirm compatibility and connectors, install safely, detect the drive, then partition/format only the intended new disk

options.label: D
options.text: Delete all partitions on both drives before shutdown

questions.rationale: Backup, compatibility and target verification should precede destructive operations.

questions.text: A legacy impact printer is required for multi-part forms, and quiet printing is also a priority. What trade-off should the technician explain?

options.label: B
options.text: A monitor can print duplicate forms

options.label: C
options.text: An optical disc is an impact printer

options.label: D
options.text: Impact printing supports multipart copies but generally makes more mechanical noise than non-impact inkjet printing

questions.rationale: Impact mechanism supports multi-part forms, but creates mechanical contact/noise.

questions.text: A PC has an image on an external monitor, but the laptop screen is black and its brightness is unchanged. Which diagnosis should be investigated first?

options.label: A
options.text: Internal display path/settings/panel connections rather than assuming the whole CPU has failed

questions.rationale: External output shows some graphics capability; internal display path is a more targeted first check.

questions.text: A hard drive is recognized by firmware but the operating system shows it as unallocated. Which interpretation is safest?

options.label: A
options.text: Unallocated status proves a failed monitor

options.label: B
options.text: The drive is definitely empty and can be formatted without checking

options.label: C
options.text: The drive may be physically detected but lack a recognized partition; verify contents before creating one

options.label: D
options.text: The BIOS becomes a keyboard port

questions.rationale: Unallocated does not guarantee the drive contains no recoverable data.

questions.text: A PC repeatedly loses boot settings after power is disconnected. Which motherboard-related area is relevant to investigate?

options.label: A
options.text: Firmware settings/CMOS battery or configuration retention

questions.rationale: Firmware settings and the RTC/CMOS battery can be related to settings retention.

questions.text: A technician receives a replacement expansion card whose connector appears to fit, but its power requirement may exceed the available PSU capacity. What should be checked?

options.label: B
options.text: Card compatibility and power requirements against the PSU's supported outputs before installation

options.label: C
options.text: Whether the HDD has a short file name

options.label: D
options.text: Whether the keyboard has a num-lock key

questions.rationale: Physical fit alone does not establish electrical/power compatibility.

questions.text: A data-transfer test shows the new drive stores more files, but large file copies complete at the same speed. Which conclusion is valid?

options.label: A
options.text: Access time and storage capacity are identical

options.label: B
options.text: Higher capacity guarantees a higher transfer rate

options.label: D
options.text: Storage capacity increased, but measured data transfer rate did not necessarily improve

questions.rationale: Capacity and transfer rate are separate properties.

questions.text: An HDD upgrade fails to appear after installation. Cables look secure, but the drive is not detected in firmware. What should be verified next?

options.label: A
options.text: Drive power/interface compatibility, connector seating and firmware settings before OS formatting steps

options.label: B
options.text: Format it from File Explorer immediately

questions.rationale: A drive must be detected at hardware/firmware level before OS partition operations.

questions.text: A PC's memory module is not listed after an upgrade, and the system is powered. What action is safest before reseating it?

options.label: C
options.text: Shut down and disconnect power, use anti-static precautions, then check module compatibility and seating

options.label: D
options.text: Pull the module out while running

questions.rationale: Memory handling should be performed with power removed and anti-static care.

questions.text: A team must diagnose slow file access. The drive has ample free space but latency is high and transfer rate is modest. Which approach is most technically sound?

options.label: A
options.text: Use printer resolution to estimate drive speed

options.label: B
options.text: Conclude capacity is the only performance metric

options.label: C
options.text: Measure access time and transfer rate separately and compare them with the workload and drive specifications

questions.rationale: Access latency and sustained transfer rate are different dimensions of storage performance.

questions.text: A PC uses a legacy parallel printer while a replacement desktop has only USB. What is the correct planning step?

options.label: A
options.text: Connect the parallel plug into HDMI

options.label: B
options.text: Assume every legacy interface is natively supported

options.label: C
options.text: Replace RAM with a printer adapter

options.label: D
options.text: Check whether a compatible parallel-to-USB interface and required driver are supported

questions.rationale: A suitable supported adapter may bridge the interfaces.

questions.text: A dual-OS installation is needed on a laptop that already contains an operating system and user data. What is the safest plan?

options.label: A
options.text: Back up, verify hardware/OS compatibility and partition layout, then configure boot selection before installation

options.label: B
options.text: Install both systems to the same partition without checking support

options.label: C
options.text: Disable all boot security permanently as the first step

options.label: D
options.text: Delete all partitions without reviewing the disk

questions.rationale: Dual-boot changes require data backup and careful partition/boot planning.

questions.text: A technician identifies an old CRT and a newer LCD monitor. Which physical operating principle distinguishes the CRT?

options.label: B
options.text: An electron beam excites phosphor on the screen

options.label: D
options.text: A flash-memory cell stores every pixel permanently

questions.rationale: CRT displays use an electron beam and phosphor.

questions.text: A computer boots, but an attached USB keyboard fails only on one front-panel port. The rear ports work. What does the evidence most strongly suggest?

options.label: B
options.text: The hard drive must be partitioned

options.label: C
options.text: The monitor uses the wrong resolution

options.label: D
options.text: A problem with that front-panel port, its cable or connection, rather than a complete keyboard failure

questions.rationale: Working keyboard on other ports narrows the issue to the affected port path.

questions.text: A laptop's fan is noisy after dust cleanup, and ventilation is clear. Which next step is the most responsible?

options.label: B
options.text: Power down and inspect fan mounting/obstruction or seek service if the noise persists

options.label: C
options.text: Format the drive to fix sound

options.label: D
options.text: Increase processor load until noise stops

questions.rationale: Persistent mechanical noise after cleaning may indicate a fan or mounting issue.

questions.text: A new hard drive must be divided into a system partition and a data partition. Which sequence is accurate at a high level?

options.label: A
options.text: Install a printer cartridge to create a file system

options.label: B
options.text: Format before deciding which disk is intended

options.label: C
options.text: Initialize/partition the intended disk as required, format each intended partition with a file system, then assign/use them

options.label: D
options.text: Change the monitor input, then create partitions

questions.rationale: The storage layout is planned before formatting and use.

questions.text: A motherboard provides a suitable slot, but the installed graphics card is not detected and needs extra power. What order should troubleshooting follow?

options.label: A
options.text: Verify card seating/slot compatibility and required power connection, then inspect firmware and drivers

questions.rationale: Physical and power conditions come before software-driver troubleshooting.

questions.text: A repair involves a power connector with male/female contacts. Why should the connector type and orientation be verified before applying power?

options.label: A
options.text: It changes the display's pixel count

options.label: B
options.text: Incorrect or mismatched power connections can damage components and create safety risks

options.label: C
options.text: It alters the keyboard language automatically

questions.rationale: Connector matching is necessary for electrical safety and hardware compatibility.

questions.text: A laptop's internal graphics card is integrated into the system board, while another model has a discrete graphics card. Which conclusion is safest?

options.label: A
options.text: A graphics subsystem changes hard-drive formatting

options.label: B
options.text: Every graphics card can be removed like a USB drive

options.label: C
options.text: Integrated graphics always require a separate display cable

options.label: D
options.text: Design and upgrade options depend on the particular laptop; a discrete card is not automatically user-replaceable

questions.rationale: Laptop upgradeability is model-specific, especially for graphics hardware.

questions.text: A disk has capacity 1 TB, but the OS displays only one 200 GB volume and the rest appears unallocated. What is the likely explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The remaining space is definitely CPU cache

options.label: C
options.text: The printer has hidden the other partitions

options.label: D
options.text: The disk may have additional unallocated space that has not been assigned to a partition/volume

questions.rationale: Unallocated capacity is not presented as a usable volume until partitioned and formatted.

questions.text: A PC will not start after a motherboard installation. The outlet works and fans spin, but no display appears. Which staged diagnostic is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Recheck internal power connectors, RAM/graphics seating and firmware/hardware indicators one change at a time

options.label: D
options.text: Format the old hard drive first

questions.rationale: A staged hardware check helps isolate assembly or seating problems.

questions.text: A computer needs a quiet printer for ordinary office documents and a separate printer for multi-part forms. Which pairing is most suitable?

options.label: B
options.text: Inkjet for quiet non-impact output; dot-matrix for impact multi-part forms

options.label: C
options.text: Dot-matrix for both because it is non-impact

options.label: D
options.text: Inkjet for multipart impact forms; HDD for paper output

questions.rationale: The two printer mechanisms serve different output constraints.

questions.text: A technician plans to format a disk because the OS cannot read its partition. What evidence should be checked first?

options.label: B
options.text: Format all connected drives to test them

options.label: C
options.text: Confirm the disk identity, backup status and whether data recovery is needed before any destructive action

options.label: D
options.text: Remove the PSU fan to improve reading

questions.rationale: An unreadable partition can still contain valuable data.

questions.text: A laptop is connected to a display through HDMI, and audio is also routed to the display. Which explanation is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: HDMI can carry digital video and audio, subject to device support and settings

options.label: B
options.text: HDMI is a magnetic storage format

options.label: C
options.text: HDMI is used only for printer ribbons

questions.rationale: HDMI supports digital audio/video.

questions.text: A workstation loses time/date settings when disconnected from mains power, but boots otherwise. Which area is worth checking?

options.label: C
options.text: RTC/CMOS battery and firmware configuration retention

questions.rationale: The motherboard's timekeeping/configuration battery may cause settings loss.

questions.text: A hardware report confuses memory capacity with disk access time. Which correction is exact?

options.label: B
options.text: Access time is the number of USB ports

options.label: C
options.text: Capacity is the speed at which a mouse moves

options.label: D
options.text: Capacity is the amount that can be stored; access time is the delay to retrieve/access data

questions.rationale: The terms measure storage quantity and latency, respectively.

questions.text: An optical drive reads a DVD but not a CD-RW. What should be checked before replacing the entire motherboard?

options.label: B
options.text: Drive support/compatibility, disc condition and the correct driver or connection path

questions.rationale: Disc format support and disc/drive condition are targeted checks.

questions.text: A technician must install a second hard drive in a desktop. Which combination must generally be available?

options.label: C
options.text: Compatible drive bay/mounting, data interface connection and suitable power connection

options.label: D
options.text: A printer ribbon and speaker grille

questions.rationale: The drive requires physical mounting and data/power connections.

questions.text: After keyboard cleaning, a key is physically stuck but the keyboard still enumerates normally. Which diagnosis is most targeted?
questions.rationale: A physically stuck key points to the keyboard mechanism.

questions.text: A drive is missing from the OS after a cable replacement. It is absent in firmware as well. Which conclusion is most justified?

options.label: A
options.text: Investigate power/data cabling, drive compatibility or hardware failure before OS partition steps

options.label: B
options.text: The display cable is definitely at fault

options.label: D
options.text: The drive only needs a file-system label

questions.rationale: If firmware cannot detect the drive, investigate hardware/power/interface first.

questions.text: A laptop overheats only when used on a blanket and works better on a hard table. Which mechanism best explains the pattern?

options.label: A
options.text: The keyboard changes the CPU's instruction set

options.label: B
options.text: The blanket may obstruct intake/exhaust airflow, reducing cooling

options.label: C
options.text: The hard table doubles RAM capacity

options.label: D
options.text: The screen resolution changes battery chemistry

questions.rationale: Blocked vents can impair cooling and raise system temperatures.

questions.text: A hard disk upgrade is required while keeping the existing operating system and documents. Which plan best balances installation and data risk?

options.label: A
options.text: Format the current drive before testing the new one

options.label: B
options.text: Disconnect the old disk while the computer is running regardless of support

options.label: C
options.text: Back up data, verify the new drive/interface, install with power disconnected, detect it, then partition/format only the new disk if required

options.label: D
options.text: Copy files after erasing the only disk

questions.rationale: The sequence protects data and avoids unnecessary destructive changes.

questions.text: A monitor works at low resolution but shows no image at a selected higher mode. What is the first sensible correction?

options.label: D
options.text: Return to a supported resolution and verify input/cable compatibility

questions.rationale: A mode beyond display/cable support can prevent a usable image.

questions.text: A technician must connect a legacy serial device and a modern USB device. Which principle governs the connection choice?

options.label: B
options.text: Match each peripheral's interface with a supported computer port/adapter and driver

options.label: C
options.text: Any connector can carry any data if forced

options.label: D
options.text: Use the monitor port for serial data

questions.rationale: Interface standards are not interchangeable without supported hardware.

questions.text: A system offers integrated graphics and a discrete expansion-card option. What should guide choosing the discrete card?

options.label: B
options.text: Whether the printer uses impact dots

options.label: C
options.text: How many partitions are on the hard disk

options.label: D
options.text: Required graphics workload, compatibility, physical fit, power and cooling capacity

questions.rationale: Graphics choice must account for workload and system limits.

questions.text: A technician has to identify whether a device is magnetic, optical or flash storage. Which trio is mapped correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: HDD—magnetic; DVD—optical; USB flash drive—flash memory

questions.rationale: The named storage devices use those technologies.

questions.text: A hard disk's measured transfer rate is good but response to many small random requests is slow. Which additional metric should be inspected?
questions.rationale: Access time helps characterize response latency for requests.

questions.text: A PC's keyboard and mouse are not detected on PS/2 ports but do work over USB. What is the most targeted next check?

options.label: D
options.text: PS/2 port/device support, port condition and firmware settings

questions.rationale: Evidence narrows the issue to the legacy PS/2 path or support.

questions.text: A repair is complete and the PC boots, but one fan remains disconnected. What should the technician do before returning the system?

options.label: A
options.text: Run a long stress test while overheated

options.label: B
options.text: Power down and reconnect/verify the fan, then test cooling and stability

options.label: D
options.text: Leave it disconnected if the PC starts

questions.rationale: Correct fan operation is important for safe and stable cooling.
